name: Single-item auctions: an asymmetric regular instance where Myerson's revenue exceeds second price with the best anonymous reserve by a factor above 2.1596 (JLTX four-buyer record)
compute_profile: laptop-hours (parameter search over 5-50 triangular buyers; certification is closed-form integrals in interval arithmetic)
statement: For independent regular buyers of one item, compare Myerson's optimal revenue OPT with second-price revenue AR under its best anonymous reserve. Jin, Lu, Tang and Xiao (SODA 2019, arXiv:1804.00480, Theorem 3) give a four-buyer triangular example with numerical ratio about 2.1596. It refutes Hartline and Roughgarden's conjecture of 2. The upper bound is the anonymous-pricing constant near 2.62. Feng and Jin (arXiv:2411.03583) describe the remaining ratio as open. The four-buyer parameters are rounded and the calculation is numerical. The proposed bar 2.1600 includes separation from that numerical value. A certificate must bound AR over every reserve, not a sampled grid.
success_criterion: An explicit instance of n >= 2 independent buyers with regular distributions, plus a certificate that a skeptic re-runs with interval or exact arithmetic, showing certified OPT/AR >= 2.1600 (higher is better). The distributions must be triangular Tri(v_i, q_i) with rational parameters (Tri(inf) allowed), or other closed-form distributions accompanied by a written regularity proof. The certificate has three parts. (a) A certified lower bound on OPT. For triangular instances sorted v_1 >= ... >= v_n this is JLTX Lemma 1: OPT = sum_i v_i q_i prod_{j<i}(1 - q_j). Otherwise use Myerson's formula with interval-certified integrals. (b) A certified upper bound on AR = sup over all reserves r >= 0 of the expected second-price revenue with anonymous reserve r. For triangular instances, JLTX Lemma 9 puts the supremum at some r = v_i, so it suffices to bound every AR(v_i) (closed-form antiderivatives or interval quadrature). For non-triangular instances, give an explicit argument covering all r. (c) The ratio of the two certified bounds is at least 2.1600. That threshold sits above JLTX's rounded 2.1596, so rounding cannot decide a claim. Re-check arXiv for any newer instance before claiming. Handle Tri(inf) through its exact limiting CDF and revenue contribution, not an undefined product of infinity and zero. Apply the finite-reserve lemma only when its hypotheses cover the proposed limiting instance; otherwise certify every reserve. Include reserve-zero and infinite-reserve endpoint limits when needed. Values in unmerged pull requests are not bars.

partial_wins.statement: The same certificate (certified OPT/AR >= 2.1600) for an instance whose distributions are quasi-regular in the sense of Feng-Jin (arXiv 2411.03583) but not all regular. This improves the upper end 0.4630 of the open quasi-regular interval AR/OPT in [0.2770, 0.4630] (Feng-Jin Result 3); that end is currently inherited from JLTX's regular instance.

verification_method: Python with mpmath interval arithmetic (or python-flint/arb), about 150 lines. For a triangular instance, write each CDF in closed form. Compute OPT by JLTX Lemma 1 exactly. For each candidate reserve v_i, compute AR(v_i) = AP(v_i) + integral from v_i to the top of (1 - D2(x)) dx, as in the proof of JLTX Theorem 3 (D2 is the CDF of the second-highest value; with a single unbounded Tri(inf) buyer the integrand vanishes above the largest finite v_i, while two or more unbounded buyers need a rigorous tail bound). Use closed-form antiderivatives of the rational integrand, or validated quadrature with rigorous tail bounds. Calibrate first on JLTX's three-buyer instance (2.1361, with the v2 equation from the proof) and on the four-buyer instance as printed (about 2.1596; record the certified value of the rounded parameters). Printed calibration outputs use tolerance within one unit of the last printed digit. The 2.1600 threshold is a numerical bar; it does not assert an exact incumbent value of 2.1596.
status_checked: 2026-10-14; historical source check from supplied batch A material. Current sources were not re-fetched during preparation.
angles: Extend JLTX's equalisation recursion. Their instances choose each new triangular buyer so that AR(v_i) = 1 at every candidate reserve while OPT grows by v_i q_i prod(1 - q_j). Add a fifth, sixth, ... buyer the same way and optimise the free parameters (2 per buyer) numerically, then certify the best point.

Treat it as an adversary problem: maximise OPT subject to AR(v_i) <= 1 for all i, a smooth nonlinear program in 2n parameters. Use multistart, then a final certified evaluation at rational parameters.

Use the conjectured infinite-buyer limit as a guide: fit the optimised (v_i, q_i) sequences for n = 4..30 and look for a continuum profile whose ratio can be computed exactly. A certified limit value would itself be a strong result.
Reading: Myerson discriminates by buyer while the anonymous reserve cannot. Worst cases pile up many small, steep-revenue buyers just below one equal-revenue whale.
pitfalls: AR is a supremum over ALL reserves. Rely on JLTX Lemma 9 only for genuinely triangular instances; otherwise certify every r.
JLTX's four-buyer parameters are printed to 4 decimals and AR ~ 1.0000 is numerical. Its certified value may differ in the 4th-5th decimal, which is why the bar is 2.1600 rather than 2.1596.
Tri(inf) has unbounded support. With one such buyer every AR integral is over a bounded range, but an instance with two or more unbounded buyers needs certified tail bounds, never truncation.
Do not confuse with anonymous PRICING (AP; tight constant C* ~ 2.62, closed), sequential posted pricing vs AP (closed) or eager/lazy personalized reserves (different cells).

Regularity must hold for each buyer. A 'buyer' made of a point mass plus a tail is regular only in the triangular form; other ad hoc mixtures can be irregular, and those count only toward the quasi-regular partial win.
